findings.claim: Outside the delta but decisive for the rehearsal this PASS authorizes: `IF projection IS DISTINCT FROM CASE max_rank WHEN 2 THEN 'level_2' WHEN 1 THEN 'level_1' ELSE 'none' END THEN` contains the exact defect class just fixed in 19-rait-priority-pre.sql — an unparenthesized SQL CASE whose `THEN` sits at parenthesis depth zero inside a PL/pgSQL IF condition. The second rehearsal's own minimal diagnostic (TASK-0028-V3-DB.md lines 72-74: `IF 1 <> CASE ... END OR false` fails to compile; the parenthesized form compiles) empirically establishes this parser behavior for the target environment. Because check_function_bodies defaults to on, CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION inf.rait_priority_consistency() will fail at DDL apply time, so the next complete dedicated rehearsal is predicted to abort at 19-rait-priority-enforce.sql inside the single transaction, wasting the rehearsal cycle. This file was never reached in either rehearsal (first aborted at 00-extensions, second at 19-pre; the legacy 49-DDL baseline excludes the three manual 19-* files), so the defect is latent, not contradicted by any recorded run. Raised now on unchanged bytes, per the R-0006 cycle rule's justification requirement, because the parser behavior making it identifiable was only established by the second rehearsal's diagnostic, after the exhaustive SQL2 cycle.
findings.fix: Before dispatching the new dedicated detran_r7_ctg1_a2 rehearsal, apply the same minimal parenthesization — `IF projection IS DISTINCT FROM (CASE max_rank WHEN 2 THEN 'level_2' WHEN 1 THEN 'level_1' ELSE 'none' END) THEN` — record the new SHA-256, and route it through the same delimited pre-parser delta review pattern; optionally verify with an isolated rolled-back `psql BEGIN; -f 19-rait-priority-enforce.sql; ROLLBACK` compile check on a disposable empty database, as was done for 19-pre.

findings.claim: Second latent instance of the same parser defect in the same unchanged file: the IF condition opened at line 203 ends with `... OR extract(year FROM age(day_on,birth)) < CASE proof->>'basis_code' WHEN 'age_80_plus' THEN 80 ELSE 60 END THEN` — the CASE sits at parenthesis depth zero (the extract() parentheses close before `< CASE`), so its `WHEN ... THEN` truncates the condition exactly like the 19-pre ELSIF did. Even after line 128 is fixed, CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION inf.rait_record_initial_priority would still fail to validate, aborting the apply transaction. All other CASE usages in the three manual 19-* files are safe: line 113 (SELECT INTO), 121 (inside EXISTS parentheses), 180 (INSERT VALUES), 207 (assignment until ';'), 219 (UPDATE) never terminate on THEN, and 19-rait-priority-verify.sql plus 34-inf-rait-case.sql contain no CASE inside IF/ELSIF conditions.
findings.fix: In the same pre-rehearsal delta as the line-128 correction, parenthesize this expression — `... < (CASE proof->>'basis_code' WHEN 'age_80_plus' THEN 80 ELSE 60 END) THEN` — so one additional delimited review covers both sites of the now-empirically-proven defect class and the rehearsal is not spent rediscovering it; no other byte of the file needs to change.

notes: Independent read-only Auditor Fable 5 review of the frozen readset CTG-0001-C4-OD-V3-PRE-PARSER-DELTA-READSET.md and native manifest ctg-0001-c4-od-v3-review-sql2-pre-parser-delta-1.manifest.json; no shell, no DB connection, no file edits, no Git. SHA-256 values were cross-checked for chain consistency across recorded artifacts, not independently recomputed: the SQL2 manifest pins the 19-pre preimage 17c97488… exactly as the readset claims; the native delta manifest pins the new 19-pre af442ccd…, an unchanged 34-inf-rait-case.sql 916bae93…, an unchanged integration spec b43efc2f…, and apply.sh 19c078cb… byte-identical to the hash pinned inside the PASS'd searchpath delta review manifest (candidate 625f74a8…, verdict PASS verified in its JSON). The only product file with a new hash in this delta is 19-rait-priority-pre.sql.

Verdict rationale for the delta itself: the parenthesization is the correct and minimal resolution of the ELSIF ambiguity. PL/pgSQL reads an IF/ELSIF condition up to the first THEN at parenthesis depth zero; the previously unparenthesized CASE placed its own THEN at depth zero, truncating the condition and leaving trailing tokens that exhaust the block — consistent with the reported first error `19-rait-priority-pre.sql:50: syntax error at end of input` and with the rolled-back minimal diagnostic and isolated single-file compile recorded in TASK-0028-V3-DB.md. Wrapping the CASE raises its THENs above depth zero so the real THEN on line 27 terminates the condition. Semantics are unchanged: `<>` already bound tighter than `OR`, and CASE is a primary expression, so `(CASE … END)` yields the identical text comparison; the notnull check via IS DISTINCT FROM on line 27, the legacy-column allowlist on lines 20-22 (rait_case agency_jurisdiction_id/judge_body_received_on/cetran_received_on plus rait_inquiry.answered_on), the FK block at lines 38-48, DDL ordering (19-pre injected before 34; 20-rls then enforce then verify last), grants, advisory lock, and the psql --single-transaction boundary are all byte-consistent with the described single-expression delta and the unchanged apply.sh.

Warning attached to this PASS: the two low findings predict that the next complete dedicated rehearsal will fail at CREATE FUNCTION time in 19-rait-priority-enforce.sql (lines 128 and 203-204 carry the same unparenthesized CASE-in-IF pattern, and that file has never been reached by any recorded apply). A PASS here authorizes the rehearsal but does not make it economical; fixing both enforce sites first via one further delimited delta (new hashes, same review pattern) is strongly recommended under ADR-0026's own token-economy direction. These findings sit on bytes unchanged since the exhaustive SQL2 cycle and are admissible per the R-0006 adjustment only because the governing parser behavior was empirically established afterward by the second rehearsal's diagnostic; they are graded low because they are outside this delta's scope and do not invalidate the reviewed change.
